overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by approving the August, October, and November 2021 minutes months late without good cause, but found the March 2021 minutes timely; ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission failed to timely approve minutes of its March 3, 2021 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: After review, we find that the Commission approved the minutes of its March 3, 2021, meeting on March 24, 2021, in compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission failed to timely approve minutes of its August 25, October 19, and November 10, 2021 meetings, approved months later.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve meeting minutes, although we note that all of the meeting minutes in question were approved before this complaint was filed with our office.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
